public_rationale: A May benchmark found substantial unresolved requirements even for its best contemporary coding system. That supports the ordinary practical reading that LLMs could not reliably perform every programming task. It does not establish permanent inability or rule out generating all the code for particular projects.
limitations: The conclusion depends on reading 'all code' as general programming coverage.
This is one preprint with a bounded task set and evaluation budget.
Failures under these conditions do not prove impossibility with unlimited retries or human assistance.

statement.excerpt: Can LLMs write all code? Not really!

our_interpretation: The ordinary practical reading is that current LLM systems cannot reliably complete every programming task correctly without human correction.
This does not mean that LLMs cannot produce useful code or complete some projects.
The observation concerns capabilities in the current month through the post date, May 1–26, 2026.
An alternative reading concerns generating every line at a particular organization. The selected reading concerns the range of programming tasks, not an organization's percentage of generated code.
criteria.support_condition: Reproducible evaluations of contemporary leading LLM coding systems identify programming tasks they cannot complete correctly under reasonable specified conditions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reproducible evidence establishes reliable autonomous completion across the claimed programming scope, including the tasks presented as counterexamples. Success on selected projects alone is insufficient.

evidence.explanation: The reported best configuration still left upgrade requirements unresolved on executable package-maintenance tasks. This supports the practical claim that contemporary systems did not reliably handle every coding task.
